levelNote: Foundational questions on the Romantic poets, novelists, prose writers and ideas.

questions.question: Which Scottish poet published Poems, Chiefly in the Scottish Dialect in 1786?
questions.explanation: Burns became celebrated after the Kilmarnock edition of his Scots-language poems appeared in 1786.

questions.question: Which paired collection by William Blake explores contrasting states of childhood and social life?
options: Songs of Innocence and of Experience
questions.explanation: Blake joined the contrasting sequences in a combined illuminated volume in 1794.

questions.question: Who wrote the lyric commonly titled I Wandered Lonely as a Cloud?
questions.explanation: Wordsworth transformed the memory of daffodils seen beside Ullswater into the lyric.

questions.question: Which poem tells of a sailor who kills an albatross and suffers a curse?
options: The Rime of the Ancient Mariner
questions.explanation: The sailor’s killing of the bird leads to supernatural punishment and eventual spiritual insight.

questions.question: Which poem made Lord Byron suddenly famous in 1812?
questions.explanation: The first two cantos brought Byron extraordinary public attention in 1812.

questions.question: Which dramatic poem by Percy Shelley features a Titan resisting tyranny?
questions.explanation: Prometheus Unbound imagines liberation through the resistance of Prometheus to oppressive authority.

questions.question: Which Keats ode sets a bird’s song against human sorrow and mortality?
questions.explanation: The song suggests a realm of imaginative joy set against suffering and passing time.

questions.question: Which Jane Austen novel features Elizabeth Bennet and Mr Darcy?
questions.explanation: The novel develops its marriage plot through misunderstandings involving Elizabeth and Darcy.

questions.question: Which novel first launched Walter Scott’s historical fiction in 1814?
questions.explanation: Waverley appeared anonymously in 1814 and began Scott’s celebrated series of historical novels.

questions.question: Who wrote Frankenstein, first published in 1818?
questions.explanation: Mary Shelley first published her Gothic and scientific novel anonymously in 1818.

questions.question: Which collection of personal writings did Charles Lamb publish in 1823?
questions.explanation: Essays of Elia gathered witty, affectionate prose pieces written under a literary persona.

questions.question: Who wrote The Spirit of the Age, a volume of contemporary literary portraits?
questions.explanation: Hazlitt examined leading writers and thinkers in his 1825 collection of portraits.

questions.question: Which poet wrote To a Mouse after disturbing a small animal while ploughing?
questions.explanation: The poem addresses a mouse whose nest has been disrupted by the speaker’s plough.

questions.question: Which Blake poem questions the creator of a fearsome striped creature?
questions.explanation: The Tyger uses the animal’s fearful symmetry to ask about creation and power.

questions.question: Which long autobiographical poem traces the growth of Wordsworth’s mind?
questions.explanation: The Prelude explores the poet’s childhood, education and mental development in blank verse.

questions.question: Which Coleridge poem was published in 1816 as a fragment associated with a dream?
questions.explanation: Kubla Khan appeared with Christabel in 1816 after an earlier period in manuscript.

questions.question: Which long satirical poem by Byron remained unfinished at his death?
questions.explanation: Don Juan uses a wandering hero and comic digressions to expose social hypocrisy.

questions.question: Which elegy did Percy Shelley compose in memory of John Keats?
questions.explanation: Adonais was written in 1821 as an elegiac response to Keats’s death.

questions.question: Which 1798 publication is conventionally used to mark the beginning of English Romanticism?
questions.explanation: Lyrical Ballads introduced a new poetic programme associated with Wordsworth and Coleridge.

questions.question: Which Keats ode reflects on images preserved on an ancient vessel?
questions.explanation: The urn presents enduring scenes that invite thought about art and human change.

questions.question: Which Austen novel follows a confident young woman whose attempts at matchmaking go wrong?
questions.explanation: Emma Woodhouse repeatedly misreads the affections and motives of those around her.

questions.question: Which Scott novel takes its readers to medieval England?
questions.explanation: Ivanhoe is a historical romance set in medieval England, unlike many of Scott’s Scottish novels.

questions.question: What is the name of the scientist who creates a living being in Frankenstein?
questions.explanation: Victor conducts the experiment and then abandons the being he has animated.

questions.question: What pen name did Charles Lamb use for his best-known magazine essays?
questions.explanation: The persona Elia enabled Lamb to write intimate, playful reflections on ordinary life.

questions.question: In which year did Hazlitt publish The Spirit of the Age?
questions.explanation: The book collected Hazlitt’s critical portraits of his contemporaries in 1825.

questions.question: Which narrative by the Scottish poet features a farmer and a frightening encounter with witches?
questions.explanation: Tam o Shanter follows a farmer who witnesses a supernatural gathering and flees.

questions.question: What technique did Blake use to print words and illustrations together from etched plates?
questions.explanation: Blake etched text and images together on copper plates and coloured impressions by hand.

questions.question: Who became Poet Laureate in 1843 after Robert Southey?
questions.explanation: Wordsworth accepted the laureateship in 1843 and held it until his death in 1850.

questions.question: Which prose work published in 1817 discusses imagination and fancy?
questions.explanation: Coleridge developed a theory of imagination and criticised aspects of Wordsworth’s poetic theory.

questions.question: In which country did Byron die while supporting a war for independence?
questions.explanation: Byron died at Missolonghi in Greece in 1824 while aiding the independence movement.

questions.question: Which Shelley poem addresses a powerful wind as an agent of change?
questions.explanation: The wind is invoked to spread the poet’s words and help bring renewal.

questions.question: What name did Keats give the ability to remain in uncertainty without impatiently seeking certainty?
questions.explanation: Keats proposed negative capability in a letter written in December 1817.

questions.question: Which was the first of Austen’s novels published in her lifetime?
questions.explanation: Sense and Sensibility appeared in 1811 under the authorial description By a Lady.

questions.question: Which literary form became especially associated with Scott’s blending of invented people and real past events?
questions.explanation: Scott made the historical novel influential by placing fictional characters in documented historical settings.

questions.question: Which lakeside gathering helped inspire the creation of Frankenstein?
questions.explanation: The group’s challenge to write ghost stories near Lake Geneva in 1816 inspired the novel.

questions.question: With which family member did Lamb collaborate on Tales from Shakespear?
questions.explanation: Charles and Mary Lamb retold Shakespearean plays in prose for young readers in 1807.

questions.question: What is the focus of Hazlitt’s 1817 book about the plays of Shakespeare?
questions.explanation: Hazlitt’s 1817 volume critically discusses the dramatic characters in Shakespeare’s plays.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the poetry of Robert Burns:
I. His Kilmarnock volume appeared in 1786.
II. He drew upon Scots speech and rural experience.
III. He died in 1832 after publishing Waverley.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Burns published his first major volume in 1786 and died in 1796; Scott wrote Waverley.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding William Blake’s writing and art:
I. Songs of Innocence appeared in 1789.
II. Songs of Experience appeared in 1794.
III. His books were normally mass-produced by newspaper presses.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Blake used his own illuminated printing method rather than normal commercial mass printing.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the early Romantic poetry collection:
I. Wordsworth and Coleridge contributed poems.
II. The first edition was edited by Walter Scott in 1814.
III. The first edition appeared in 1798.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: The 1798 volume was the work of Wordsworth and Coleridge, not Scott.

questions.question: Which poet explained the idea of a willing suspension of disbelief?
questions.explanation: Coleridge used the phrase while reflecting on supernatural poetry and its readers.

questions.question: What term describes the proud, brooding and rebellious outsider associated with Byron’s poetry?
questions.explanation: The Byronic hero combines charisma, defiance and often a burden of hidden guilt.

questions.question: Which prose essay by Shelley was written in 1821 and published posthumously?
questions.explanation: A Defence of Poetry argues for the imaginative and moral significance of poets.

questions.question: Which emphasis most strongly distinguishes Romantic writing from much Augustan poetry?
questions.explanation: Romantic writers often foreground imaginative vision, nature and personal experience.

questions.question: Which poet died in Rome in 1821 at the age of twenty-five?
questions.explanation: Keats died of tuberculosis in Rome after travelling to Italy for his health.

questions.question: Which Austen novel gently satirises a heroine’s enthusiasm for Gothic fiction?
questions.explanation: Catherine Morland misreads ordinary events through expectations learned from Gothic stories.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding Walter Scott’s career:
I. He first gained fame as a poet.
II. Waverley was originally published without his name.
III. He became Poet Laureate in 1813.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Scott declined the laureateship, which went to Robert Southey; his earliest novels appeared anonymously.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding Mary Shelley’s early fiction:
I. The novel was published anonymously at first.
II. The Last Man was published before the turn of the eighteenth century.
III. Frankenstein appeared in 1818.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Frankenstein was issued without Mary Shelley’s name, while The Last Man came later in 1826.

questions.question: In which periodical were Lamb’s Elia essays originally published?
questions.explanation: Lamb’s familiar essays appeared in the London Magazine before collection in book form.

questions.question: Which series collected Hazlitt’s conversational essays in the early 1820s?
questions.explanation: Table-Talk gathered Hazlitt’s literary and social essays in a familiar prose style.
